svg.text: interview entry point — wraps exactly ONE service
createAuction(itemId, sellerId, startPrice, start, end): id
placeBid returns a BOOLEAN, not an exception —
being outbid is a normal outcome, not an error ✓
but self-bidding DOES throw — that is fraud, not a loss
the seam — swap in a persistent impl unchanged
shutdown() on the interface is a smell (lifecycle leaking into
the API) — AutoCloseable would say it better
THE CORE — service + the synchronized aggregate
expireAuctions() every 1s: ACTIVE && now > endTime → auction.end()
maps are for LOOKUP only — every mutation goes through
id, itemId, sellerId, startTime, endTime (all final)
price, winner and bid list can never diverge — one monitor guards all three
THE STATE PATTERN + the bid model
ActiveAuctionState → the only state that accepts bids
bidding rules live in ONE class, not an if-ladder ✓
honest: a MANUAL bid only has to beat
currentPrice — bidIncrement is NOT enforced here
which is what proxy counter-bids step by
one-line fix: compare against nextMinimumBid() instead
honest: OUTBID is declared but never set —
"bid for me up to X" — the service does the bidding
one proxy per bidder per auction (a Map, not a list)
registering a proxy immediately fires a bid if
1. skip the bidder who just bid
2. among the rest, keep proxies whose
Ana proxy max 500 · Bo proxy max 300
this is second-price-ish behaviour: you pay just
enough to beat the runner-up, not your own cap
exactly what eBay-style proxy bidding promises
• the proxy scan runs OUTSIDE the auction
monitor — read-then-bid is not atomic, so a
racing manual bid can make a counter stale
• it recurses through placeBid — a deep
proxy war grows the stack; a loop is safer
• expiry polls every second — up to 1s of
late bids can still land after endTime
(placeBid re-checks the clock, so no bid is wrongly accepted)
every accepted bid triggers a proxy resolution pass

auction lies about who is winning.
Three atomics would each be safe and
One monitor per auction means a
hot listing serialises all its bidders.
That is correct and usually fine —
the critical section is a compare and
Different auctions never contend at all.
